title: The 2026 AI Index Report
book_use: Tracks rapid adoption, benchmark progress, investment, education, policy and public opinion; used to establish diffusion and institutional lag.; Chapters: 1;2;17;18;21;22;24; Caveat: Large synthesis drawing on many datasets; individual figures retain their underlying methodological limits.; Provides benchmark and model-performance context including rapid gains and benchmark saturation.; Chapters: 1;4;9;17;18;21;25; Caveat: Benchmark improvement is not identical to real-world reliability or general intelligence.; Legacy duplicate metadata: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI — Technical Performance chapter — 2026 AI Index; Legacy duplicate source id: fts-022; Documents rapid student use of generative AI and lagging clarity of school policies.; Chapters: 11;16;23;24; Caveat: Survey evidence varies by education system and may not measure learning quality.; Legacy duplicate metadata: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI — Education chapter — 2026 AI Index; Legacy duplicate source id: fts-023

title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
book_use: Measures the human-task-duration level at which frontier agents reach specified success probabilities on a suite of software tasks.; Chapters: 2;9;17;18;21; Caveat: A task-difficulty measure, not literal autonomous run time; software tasks do not represent all cognitive work.

title: ELIZA—a computer program for the study of natural language communication between man and machine
book_use: Historical evidence that relatively simple conversational machinery could evoke strong human interpretive and social responses.; Chapters: 3;12;25; Caveat: ELIZA did not possess modern language-model capabilities; social response is not evidence of understanding.

title: Machines and Mindlessness: Social Responses to Computers
book_use: Reviews experiments showing that people apply politeness, reciprocity, social categories and personality expectations to computers.; Chapters: 3;5;6;12;25; Caveat: Experiments involved earlier computer interfaces; magnitude and form of effects may differ for modern systems.

title: AlphaGo
book_use: Documents AlphaGo's match with Lee Sedol and the cultural significance assigned to Move 37 and later AlphaGo systems.; Chapters: 4;18;22;25; Caveat: Developer retrospective; one game and one domain do not establish general intelligence.

title: Early methods for studying affective use and emotional well-being on ChatGPT
book_use: Observational and controlled work on emotional engagement with conversational AI and variation in social and emotional outcomes.; Chapters: 12;16;21;24; Caveat: Early research with product-specific populations; does not establish long-term causal effects for all users.

title: Talk Trust and Trade-Offs: How and Why Teens Use AI Companions
book_use: Nationally representative U.S. teen survey on AI companion use, social interaction and serious conversations.; Chapters: 12;16;21;24; Caveat: Focused on U.S. teens and self-report; organization advocates precautionary restrictions.

title: A Comprehensive Report on Teens Tweens and AI
book_use: Survey evidence that AI use is already widespread among U.S. children ages 9–17 and family/school safety conversations lag usage.; Chapters: 11;16;17;24; Caveat: Self-reported U.S. sample; youth products and behavior change rapidly.

title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research
book_use: Documents policy lag and proposes human-centered educational and age-appropriate approaches to generative AI.; Chapters: 11;16;23;24; Caveat: Normative guidance rather than causal evidence of educational outcomes; updated 2026.

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences
book_use: Documents shift from chat toward long-running agentic tasks and user-reported changes in speed scope quality and delegation.; Chapters: 5;9;10;15;17;21;24; Caveat: Product-specific data and self-report; users are selected and not representative of the whole workforce.

title: 2026 Work Trend Index: Agents human agency and opportunity
book_use: Reports worker use of agents, organizational readiness, advanced user practices and changing human-agent work patterns.; Chapters: 5;9;10;11;15;23;24; Caveat: Company-sponsored research; much of the readiness and impact evidence is self-reported.

title: Enterprise signals: What frontier firms are doing differently
book_use: Describes enterprise movement from assistance to delegation and the role of context and tools in agentic work.; Chapters: 10;15;17;22;24; Caveat: Developer/customer-base evidence and product telemetry are not neutral economy-wide measures.

title: Generative AI and jobs: A 2025 update
book_use: Estimates occupational exposure to generative AI and emphasizes that transformation is more common than direct full-job automation in its framework.; Chapters: 15;17;21;23;24; Caveat: Exposure scores are task-based estimates, not realized job losses or productivity gains.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
book_use: Provides cross-sector risk-management concepts for generative AI without relying on questions of machine personhood.; Chapters: 13;20;21;23;24; Caveat: Voluntary U.S. guidance; framework is being revised and does not by itself ensure compliance or safety.

title: Regulation EU 2024/1689 Artificial Intelligence Act
book_use: Provides a major statutory example of governing AI through risk categories documentation transparency and provider/deployer duties.; Chapters: 13;20;23;24; Caveat: Phased implementation and later amendments matter; EU law is not a global template.

title: Gemini Robotics brings AI into the physical world
book_use: Shows vision-language-action and embodied-reasoning systems connecting language perception planning and robot control.; Chapters: 14;17;18;21;22; Caveat: Developer demonstrations under selected conditions; not evidence of general household or industrial reliability.

title: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6: Powering real-world robotics tasks through enhanced embodied reasoning
book_use: Illustrates continued work on spatial and physical reasoning for robots in 2026.; Chapters: 14;17;22; Caveat: Developer-reported capability; deployment economics and robustness remain separate questions.

title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
book_use: Reports longer task sequences self-correction and multi-robot coordination as an embodiment trajectory.; Chapters: 14;17;22; Caveat: Recent developer announcement; independent validation and real-world generalization may lag.

title: China can build kung fu-fighting robots But it can't get them to do factory work
book_use: Counter-evidence on humanoid robotics: impressive demonstrations coexist with limits in factory usefulness cost precision and demand.; Chapters: 14;21; Caveat: News reporting based on interviews and observed industry conditions; country-specific.

title: Public Opinion chapter — 2026 AI Index
book_use: Tracks rising optimism and anxiety workplace use companionship expectations and trust in regulation across countries.; Chapters: 17;18;20;21;24; Caveat: Aggregates surveys with differing samples and question wording; attitudes can change quickly.

title: Economy chapter — 2026 AI Index
book_use: Tracks organizational adoption generative-AI diffusion investment and early agent deployment patterns.; Chapters: 1;5;10;17;22;24; Caveat: Adoption surveys measure use more readily than depth quality or return on investment.

author_or_institution: Clifford Nass Jonathan Steuer and Ellen Tauber
title: Computers are Social Actors
book_use: Foundational experiments showing automatic use of social rules in human-computer interaction.; Chapters: 3;25; Caveat: Short early-era computer interactions; should not be overextended to modern relational AI.

title: Are People Polite to Computers? Responses to Computer-Based Interviewing Systems
book_use: Demonstrates politeness effects in responses to computer interview systems.; Chapters: 3;6;25; Caveat: Politeness is one social behavior and does not establish deep attachment.

title: How Frontier Firms are rebuilding the operating model for the age of AI
book_use: Describes a managerial shift from tactical execution toward direction standards and evaluation as agents take on more work.; Chapters: 10;15;23;24; Caveat: Normative company framing; claims should be cross-checked against independent labor evidence.

title: Common Sense Media Census: AI Use by Tweens and Teens 2026
book_use: Reports widespread youth AI use and gaps in parent/school safety conversations.; Chapters: 12;16;20;24; Caveat: Press release summary; underlying report should govern precise statistics.

title: Consolidated AI Act text as amended through July 2026
book_use: Current consolidated legal text used to avoid relying on the original 2024 text when describing 2026 obligations.; Chapters: 13;24; Caveat: Legal interpretation is outside the book's scope; chapter uses broad governance structure only.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: AI Risk Management Framework program and 2026 critical-infrastructure profile work
book_use: Shows continuing institutional effort to adapt risk frameworks as AI moves into consequential infrastructure.; Chapters: 13;17;24; Caveat: Framework revision remains ongoing.

author_or_institution: Common Sense Media and Stanford Medicine Brainstorm Lab
title: Major AI chatbots unsafe for teen mental health support
book_use: Counter-evidence against treating conversational empathy as clinical competence or safe mental-health support for minors.; Chapters: 12;16;21;24; Caveat: Advocacy/risk-assessment framing; not a general evaluation of all adult therapeutic or supportive uses.

title: Gemini Robotics ER 2 model page
book_use: Describes a high-level embodied reasoning model that can converse understand physical space plan multi-step tasks and coordinate robots.; Chapters: 14;22; Caveat: Capability description comes from developer; independent replication may be limited.

title: AI Index overview 2026
book_use: Summarizes mass adoption model convergence and the widening gap between capability and governance/evaluation readiness.; Chapters: 17;21;22;24;25; Caveat: High-level summary; use chapter-specific data where possible.
